title: ground-loop-is-discoverable-without-scanning
intention: The ground loop is discoverable by address rather than by scanning — liveness, status, and registry collapse into one mechanism.
why: Three things collapse into one mechanism. (a) 'start it only if it isn't running' needs a liveness answer; (b) 'show me the ground loop's state' needs the same answer; (c) the NO DAEMONS law's actual WHY — UU grew daemons willy-nilly and shutting them down was unreliable — is served by exactly this: the one sanctioned resident process becomes accountable and discoverable by construction. The touch-file does not weaken NO DAEMONS, it is what makes the single permitted exception honest.
traces_to: Law 3 — nothing is known until measured: discovery without scanning IS measurement
Law 4 — enforced by physics: the mechanism replaces a periodic scan with a discoverable address

falsifier.proves_red: A liveness read disagrees with reality, in EITHER direction: (1) the record says LIVE and no loop is running (a stale record after an unclean death — the start-guard then refuses to start and the system is silently dead); (2) the record says DEAD and a loop IS running (two entry points each start one, and every callback fires twice). Direction (2) is the expensive one and is the reason presence-of-file cannot be the test.
falsifier.horizon: Readable within one session for direction (2) — race it deliberately. Direction (1) needs a real unclean death, which is why it carries a WATCHME rather than a proof alone: a proof can SIMULATE a stale record, but only time tells us what threshold is honest.

intent_verbatim: superclaude is one of the entry points that will start the ground loop but only if it's not already running. I also propose that the ground loop has a file it touches on each pass. can be in it's device space in .cairn. that shows us it's last run without scanning for the process. if we were really smart we'd put it's state in there too... and then when the web server displays the ground loop state in it's device, it's process ID would be present. process id as part of the base shim device status pane too.
intent: The one resident process in Cairn reports its own liveness, so nothing has to go looking for it. The loop writes a record on each pass — last-run, state, pid — in its own device space. Every consumer (a start-guard, a status pane, a human) READS that record instead of scanning the process table. Liveness stops being a host question and becomes an owned fact (Law 6).

gate_findings.assumption_1: The ground loop is a RESIDENT PROCESS. Checked against NO DAEMONS and it is a distinction, not a collision: I-heartbeat-probes-and-bus.md already names the ground loop as 'the one permitted periodic pulse, and it exists precisely so that nothing else has to be.'
gate_findings.assumption_2_FALSE_AS_STATED: 'A file that is touched tells us the loop is running.' It does not — a crashed loop leaves the file behind. Akien's own design supplies the fix without connecting it: the record carries LAST RUN, so liveness is 'touched within N beats', not 'file exists'. Connecting those two halves is this ticket's real content.
gate_findings.missing_2_the_race: Two entry points reading 'not running' at the same moment both start a loop. Read-then-act is not atomic; the claim must be (O_EXCL create, or equivalent). Carried by the child that owns the guard.
gate_findings.falsifiable: yes — stated above, both directions, with a horizon.
gate_findings.collides: Checked four ways, no collision. NO DAEMONS: distinction (above). reaching-for-daemons-is-drift: a per-pass touch is the loop recording itself, not a poller; a reader that POLLED the file would be the drift, and every reader here is event-driven (a browser request, a launch). Law 6: the ground loop owns the file, in its own device space. system_rackmount owns host-resource predicates — and this design never asks the host anything, which sidesteps that ownership question rather than crossing it.
gate_findings.verdict: CAST. The two missing points are specifiable implementation decisions, not open design, so they are named on the ticket rather than routed back. If Akien reads the staleness threshold as a design question, this reverts to a red and the parent goes back to THINKME.

gate_findings.assumption_2_CORRECTED_2026-07-31: SUPERSEDED. I recorded this as 'a file that is touched tells us the loop is running — FALSE AS STATED.' Akien: 'a crashed loop does leave the file behind: BUT IT STOPS UPDATING THE TIMESTAMP. So then it's possible to DETECT that it's not running and start it.' Correct, and the detector was already in his design — he specified last-run in the file before I raised anything. The honest word was UNDERSPECIFIED, not false: the design was one number short, and the number is 5 seconds. Recording the miss because it is the third of a kind — I reach for the strong word (conflict, false) where the honest one is 'not yet specified'. the_threshold: THE STALENESS THRESHOLD IS 5 SECONDS — five missed ticks at the ruled once-per-second cadence. Ruled by Akien 2026-07-31. Three times the interval is the standard liveness heuristic; five gives slack for a loaded box without anyone noticing the lag. LIVE = last-run within 5s. DEAD = last-run older than 5s, whatever the file says about state, whatever pid it names. A crashed loop leaves the file behind but STOPS ADVANCING THE TIMESTAMP — that is the whole detector, and it is Akien's, present in the design from the first telling.
filed_edges: [AKIEN] WHAT IS THE STALENESS WINDOW, AND WHERE DOES IT COME FROM? This parent's falsifier says presence-of-file cannot be the test because the expensive direction is 'record says DEAD while a loop is running'. Its child an-entry-point-starts-the-loop-only-once already assumes a number — 'a loop alive but merely slow is declared dead inside the 5s window' — and nothing says where 5s came from or what happens on a loaded machine. One number gates all three children, and getting it wrong in the cheap direction stalls the system while getting it wrong in the expensive direction doubles every callback.

[CORPUS] IS THE LIVENESS RECORD THE SAME RECORD AS a-record-reaches-disk's LAYER 0? That ticket needs a writer that runs on its own rather than a proof calling in, and this cluster is building exactly that. If they are one record, these are one build; if two, we are about to write the system's first two disk records in parallel and should say why.
